captions.fig1_naming_turn: NAME titles (coined name before a colon or spaced dash) rose from 20.3% of ICLR submissions in 2023 to 40.5% in 2026 on a trend already running since 2017 (pre-trend OR 1.125/yr), and the camera-ready-free pool (rejected, withdrawn, desk-rejected; 40.3% in 2026) tracks all submissions. (a) The 2024 slope change is OR 1.098 [1.044, 1.154]/yr at paper level but 1.096 [0.990, 1.214] with year-level inference (NA pool 1.121 [1.019, 1.232]); only 2026 departs from the extrapolated 2017-23 trend (+5.5 pp [1.5, 9.5]). Aqua: name-masked abstract content counterfactuals (dotted line R1 fixed window; ribbon = range over R1/R3/R5 in the fixed and rolling designs), which explain 0.38-0.58 of the 2023-26 rise; the placebo window (trained 2018-20) already under-predicts 2021-23. (b) Annual change split into the part predicted by a rolling R1 content model and the unexplained part u; mean u rose by +1.35 pp (two-stage year-level 95% CI [0.03, 2.71]; year-label permutation p = 0.14).
captions.fig2_decomposition: Shares of the 2023-26 rise in NAME titles (Δ = 20.2 pp) attributed to abstract content, team composition and detectable LLM drafting; grey bands are the pre-registered predictions (content 0.20-0.50, composition ≤ 0.30, tool < 0.25). Name-masked content explains 0.38-0.49 in the fixed window and 0.56-0.58 in the rolling design, so 'content is a minority' is not established. Team size x new keys x LLM topic explains 0.26 by DFL reweighting but 0.09 net of content (Shapley). Detectable LLM drafting at A_max = 0.39 accounts for 7.1% [1.4, 12.9] after misclassification correction (3.1% by the pre-registered formula), but alternative fingerprints give up to 33%, so the tool share is small for the abstract fingerprint, not bounded in general. The Shapley residual (unexplained by content or composition) is 0.57 [0.53, 0.62]. Content and composition CIs: conditional paper bootstrap (models fixed), B = 2000; tool-share CIs propagate the 95% CI of the fingerprint uplift δ.
captions.fig3_carriers: Who carries the NAME rise between E = 2022-23 and L = 2025-26 (declared profile keys; list position is a partition label only). (a) NAME change on papers grouped by how new their keys are, as a ratio of the population change (key-cluster bootstrap 95% CIs; right column: L-period papers). Papers whose keys are all stayer keys changed 0.06 [-0.14, 0.28] times the population change, papers whose keys all appeared in an earlier year 0.66 [0.49, 0.85], and last-position stayer keys on papers with an entrant first key 1.14 [1.07, 1.20]: the rise is graded by team newness. The pooled stayer-to-population ratios (ρ_last 0.995, ρ_any 0.816) are not identified as communal change, because a purely generational world with the observed co-authorship would give 0.78-0.93. (b) Generational increment G = 1 - slope of within-stayer on population change across 52 title style and 33 abstract topic markers: style markers move more slowly among stayer keys than topic markers (any position: G_style 0.17 [0.13, 0.20] vs G_topic -0.05 [-0.07, -0.03]), and the gap sits at the first list position (G_style 0.40). Holm p: H2a 0.005, H2b 0.005, H2d 0.005.
captions.fig4_register: LLM-favoured wording in titles. (a) Share of titles that fill a meaning-fixed opener slot with the LLM-favoured verb (Enhancing/Boosting vs Improving; Unveiling vs Understanding; Leveraging vs Exploiting; comprehensive vs systematic), pooled over slots, against control pairs (towards/toward, novel/new, via/using) in grey; bands are 95% Wilson intervals. The slot share moved from 0.34 in 2023 to 0.54 in 2024 (post OR 2.18 [1.41, 3.38] with slot-specific trends; controls 0.87 [0.64, 1.18]; slot-minus-control OR 2.55 [1.53, 4.25]); the 2023 cohort already deviates, so the break is better read as an acceleration from 2024. (b) Title rates of the 2024-generation register R24 (enhanc*, leverag*, unveil*, ...) and the 2026-generation register R26 (unified, unifying, beyond, bridging): from 2025 to 2026 R24 fell from 63.1 to 47.8 per 1,000 (down in 14/16 large areas) while R26 rose from 23.3 to 46.4 (up in 16/16). (c) Association of an abstract LLM fingerprint (F24 ∪ F26 ∪ title typography) with the LLM slot variant and with a NAME title on the same slot-filled papers, within topic100 x year (implied ORs from LPMs, 95% CIs): OR_slot 1.42 [1.14, 1.79] vs OR_NAME 0.91 [0.72, 1.16], ratio 1.55 [1.11, 2.21] (n = 1,506 papers, 2024-26). Holm p: H3a <0.001, H3b 0.004, H3d 0.005.
captions.fig5_stage_gains: Stage gains P(feature | passed stage) / P(feature | entered stage) for ICLR 2024-26 (year-standardised; paper bootstrap stratified by year, B = 2000, 95% CIs). (a) Desk screen, author exit (withdrawal before decision) and decision, and their product, the accepted/all ratio. NAME is slightly depleted before the decision (exit 0.974 [0.965, 0.983]) and enriched at it (decision 1.050 [1.028, 1.072]), netting to 1.021 (90% CI 1.001-1.041, inside the [0.90, 1.11] equivalence margin); the 2024 slope break is similar in accepted, rejected and withdrawn pools (ORs 1.05 / 1.12 / 1.11, equality p = 0.51). Outsider markers are depleted (0.807 [0.749, 0.870]), mostly at the decision stage, where camera-ready reformatting cannot be excluded; LLM-style markers mildly so (0.975 [0.951, 1.001]). (b) Accepted/all ratio by year (grey band: the pre-registered [0.95, 1.10] band for NAME). The LLM-style union was enriched among accepted papers in 2018-23 (1.154 [1.070, 1.236]) and is not after 2023. Decision-stage gains are not identified against camera-ready edits (Figure 6b).
captions.fig6_published_bias: How far a study of accepted papers alone would be from the full submission pool (2024-26). (a) Accepted-only / all-submission ratio for 24 pre-registered fashion statistics (95% CIs; grey band ±10%). Mainstream statistics are within ±10% in 11/11 cases (median |log ratio| 0.018); deviations concentrate in outsider (1/4 within) and LLM-style markers (7/9); the accepted-only Kobak-style LLM bound is 0.72 of the all-submission bound. (b) arXiv camera-ready audit (pre-decision v1 vs stored title, or abstract for F24; accepted minus rejected net flips; 331 pairs; auditable features only; grey: the 'via' control word): the decision-stage gain of a feature is identified only if its tipping point D* lies outside the 95% CI. For NAME the DiD is +2.09 pp [-3.16, 7.33] against D* = 2.92 pp; 0 of 24 title features pass (10 auditable); identified under any spec: none. Acceptance associations of title features are therefore associational and not separated from camera-ready editing.
captions.table1_hypotheses: Pre-registered hypotheses H1a-H4e and the decision-stage gate: prediction, regenerated estimate with 95% CI, verdict under the pre-registered falsification rule, and Holm-adjusted one-sided p within each direction.
captions.table2_acceleration: The NAME acceleration across pools, subsets, years and NAME definitions: segmented-logit slope change (primary 1.098 [1.044, 1.154]), its year-level analogue, the LPM slope change, and the acceleration of content-unexplained drift Δu.
captions.table3_content_bracket: Content-counterfactual bracket: share of the NAME rise predicted by each abstract representation (name-masked R1/R3/R5, coarse and leaky brackets) in the fixed, rolling and placebo designs, with out-of-sample AUC and the implied acceleration of unexplained drift.
captions.table4_filter_audit: Stage-wise filter gains (desk, exit, decision, total) for mainstream, outsider and LLM-style features in 2024-26, with the camera-ready audit's net-flip DiD and tipping point for each auditable feature.
